item: Recursive Hilbert-ball coloring of dyadic partitions, driven by a fixed-point-free Lipschitz map
for: Highest item confidence in the pass. Six earlier claimed proofs (Shavgulidze, Akhmedov ×2, Beklaryan, Moore 2012, Wajnryb–Witowicz) never used vector-valued or recursive invariants. A one-line definition turns a 50-year-old problem into about two pages: the Cook–Reckhow profile.
against: Unrefereed; Lean not built. The definition's own reach is narrow: groups that contain F get nonamenability from the theorem, not from the device. The fixed-point-free map itself is transfer (Benyamini–Sternfeld).
next_test: Re-run the device directly on Farey or n-adic cells for Monod's H(A) and Lodha–Moore G_0, without embedding F, and derive an explicit Kesten-norm bound for F. Negative controls must fail: the amenable IET subgroups and family 253's polygon-exchange group.
verdict: The closest match in the corpus to the extension-variable profile. The colour p(T) is a defined object that is absent from the statement and exists only to drive the proof. It dissolves a real obstruction: Følner sets control only averages of bounded functions, while the natural invariant (depth) is unbounded, so the proof needs a bounded invariant that never stabilises. Its ingredient, the Benyamini–Sternfeld map, is transfer (N0). The coupling to F's self-similarity has no precedent found, and six earlier claimed proofs never used a vector-valued recursive invariant, so it looks hard to construct. Two things stand between this and a confirmed jump. (a) The proof is unrefereed and the Lean has not been built; if the proof is wrong the item is void. (b) The strict definition needs speedups on OTHER theorems, and the definition's own reach looks narrow: groups that contain F inherit nonamenability from the theorem, not from the device, so they test nothing. It may be a one-problem key rather than a jump.

item: Thermal noisy labels Z = Y + θ (L log L Fourier convergence)
for: No earlier equivalent of the full device. Best downstream target is genuinely different: Bourgain's multi-frequency lemma.
against: Every ingredient is precedented: stochastic localization, Tao's entropy decrement, Russo–Zou, von Mises noise. It reads as a new bridge rather than a new concept. The Lean GridBound fixes the signs ε_j that the paper's Prop dyadic quantifies over, so the formal proof may not certify the label's step.
next_test: Bourgain's multi-frequency lemma in a finite model. Lowering its log²N loss toward log N would be a speedup on a different, 35-year-old theorem and would confirm the item. Run the Walsh L log L case first as a cheap check, and check whether the ε_j specialisation in the Lean matters.
verdict: F1-shaped: it adjoins a new auxiliary variable, like an extension variable. Under the strict rule, though, the mechanism is mostly transfer. Stochastic localization with the I-MMSE chain rule, Tao's entropy decrement and Russo–Zou information budgets already say 'pay for many adaptively chosen statistics with one information budget'. The new part is the instantiation in Fourier analysis: ferromagnetic thermal noise makes character decoding exact and independent of the number of frequencies. That reads as a new bridge (N2) unless the speedup test shows it does something those templates cannot. Lean caveat: the formal GridBound fixes the signs ε_j that the paper's Prop dyadic quantifies over, so the Lean may not certify the step the label exists for. It has the lowest prior here but the highest value of information, because its downstream test is concrete and would be decisive.
lean_status: formalized; Lean fixes the ε_j signs (special case of Prop dyadic)
